text: Emissaries of the Estalian Inquisition, these iron-willed dignitaries have free rein and unshackled consciences.
The wealthy and shrewd entrepreneurs of Tilea can gather large military forces around them, not by the might of the sword but by the amount of money they can shift around them.
Father and master figures of their troops, these commanders are the saviour the Borderlands need but perhaps do not deserve.
Prince Borgio of Miragliano is one of the greatest Condottieri to ever lead a Tilean army. Strong in will, charisma and limb, he might even be the one to unite the City States.
Under the illusory façade of a mysterious, disfigured yet benevolent prince, Gashnag is the last spiritual heir of Ushoran, the Strigoi patriarch.
The most beautiful lady in the entire Old World and former ruler of Pavona, Lucrezzia is a dangerous woman, proficient in magic, intrigue and poison.
One of the most powerful princes and skilled duellists in Tilea, Catrazza is a multi-faceted leader that knows how to balance politics and direct warfare.
Ostentatious, cruel, but by no means unsubtle and inefficient.
A young yet promising and brave prince of the borderlands, Valmir is both an empathic leader and a tenacious fighter.
Priestesses and Knights at once, the high-ranking officers of the Order of the Eagle are expert fighters and unrivalled tacticians.
El Cadavo, or whichever his true name is: leader of men, mercenary lord and legendary explorer. Stubborness, talent and greed in one gritty figure.
The man who had "discovered" Lustria (no matter Losteriksson or even the Lizardmen) is Prince of Trantio, explorer, marksman and diplomat.
Accursed by the Kings of Nehekhara, a long-lost Sunscryer marches again, as cantankerous as the day he died. Truly, there is no rest for the wicked.
Tilea and Estalia are home to some of the best duellists in the Old World, never long in one place if money, whims and desires have a say in it.
Mercenary generals are powerful individuals of various origins, from Princes to former soldiers, with the wealth and usually the know-how to employ armies of militias and mercenaries.
Mercenary captains are usually found leading companies of local troops or mercenaries, generally trying to make sure they get paid and not maimed too much.
The Prince of Luccini is an eccentric yet inspiring commander, with the appearance of his ancestors and the fighting prowess of a laughing daemon.
Like Piggolo I of Tobaro, Prince Piggolo II is destined to lead his followers to a new golden age.

Borgio, Prince of Miragliano, nicknamed “The Besieger” because of his unsurpassed expertise in siege warfare, is one of the greatest Mercenary Generals of his age if not in the entire Tilean history. It is said that no Tilean city, not even the ingenious ramparts of Miragliano itself, could defy him. Borgio is certainly an expert tactician and has so far won most of his battles.\\n\\nDuring his career, Borgio fought against every other principality and republic in Tilea for one reason or another, from wars over trading rights to pure vendettas against rival Princes who had tried to have him assassinated. Indeed, there were so many failed attempts to assassinate Borgio, some of which came very close to success, that he gained a reputation as a man who had to be killed more than once to be sure. The latest attempt included a treacherous toasting fork, and words of Borgio's death spread wide and far before he could walk again, with a new hatred for forked utensils.\\n\\nIt is said that Borgio once defeated an Orc horde by splitting them into three parts. Opinion is divided as to whether this refers to the horde or the individual Orcs. It is also said that Borgio could ride a horse, go to sleep and read a book at the same time.\\n\\nA student of Myrmidian tactics, Borgio implemented many strategic techniques, from employing cunning ruses in battle to inspiring his troops by leading by example and even mucking in with the construction of moats and earthworks. \\n\\nBorgio has many enemies, but quite a few valuable allies. The normally-scheming Lucrezzia Belladonna is one of his most solid friends, through Dolchellata, her sister and Borgio's wife. But most of all it is his own troops who lay an unbreachable faith in the Prince, such is his inspiring presence and track record for success. In particular, Vespero's duellists and Braganza's Besiegers are constant presences in his army and proved restless during his disappearance.

The Border Principalities are wild lands ruled over by dozens of robber barons and petty nobles. These small provinces war frequently, and are beset by the greenskins from the south. Yet there is one town, protected by a soaring dark citadel, which has survived trials and tribulations of the Borderlands for many centuries, outliving many of the longest-ruling dynasties of the region. This small kingdom is the domain of Gashnag, the Black Prince, scion of ancient Strygos. A child-in-darkness of Vorag, Gashnag is determined not to make the same mistakes of his sire. \\n\\nWhile other Vampires of the Strigoi claw an existence in the filth of old crypts, dreaming of glories past, Gashnag has quite-literally raised himself from the sewers. \\n\\nHe rose to notoriety slowly, and he has borrowed from the Lahmians the gifts of subtle manipulation. Resisting his brethren’s taste for being worshipped as Gods, he has instead recast himself as a romantic hero. Through his agents, Gashnag has paid bards and troubadours to spread the tales of his greatness across the Old World and as far afield as Araby. The rumors say that he is under a terrible curse that causes him to appear beastly and savage but that he was once strikingly handsome. These fanciful tales speak of a dashing prince, disinherited from his fortune, who seeks a loved one to provide him with an heir. It is perhaps best not to speak of what Gashnag would do should a suitable lady of breeding declare her interest.\\n\\n Under the sobriquet "The Black Prince," he appears on his battlements only at night or under layers of Ulgu enchantments and knightly disguises, ever-stoking the mystique that surrounds him.\\n\\nGashnag also saves all his violence for the enemies of his tiny kingdom, and the only time he does appear in public, his hideous form is hidden beneath a huge and heavy cloak as he swiftly rides to mete out justice or defend the borders. When a gang of Ogres from the Black Mountains began raiding villages under his protection, Gashnag immediately rode into the mountains alone. He returned the next night with a dozen heads on a spike, which he planted in the village square, so his people would know they were safe again. \\n\\nThe combination of dedicated security, and romantic allusions has caused the province to swell in population in recent years. If this continues, The Black Prince may very well succeed where his sire failed and return the Strigoi to a great power once again — and one far closer to the Empire.

Lucrezzia Belladonna is reputed, at least by her Tilean compatriots, the most beautiful woman in the Old World. She is also, quite noticeably, an accomplished wielder of magic and a powerful figure in the political landscape; a feared woman whose enemies and husbands whose usefulness seemed to be diminished are prone to suddenly falling prey to a quick and painful death, usually but not limitedly after suffering small cuts or meals. Anybody with good sense will try to stay out of her way, and to watch the rings on her hands carefully.\\n\\nAfter the fateful death of her seventh husband, Lucrezzia consolidated her alliance with the great Borgio of Miragliano through her sister. However, the ruintion of her city Pavona to a horde of unchecked Greenskins temporarily left her with no solid power base. Adaptable as ever, Lucrezza saw to secure a niche for her in Bilbali, over in Estalia, where her skills and talent for diplomacy may serve well to not only consolidate one of the best ports in the Old World as her own base, but to extend beyond it.\\n\\nAll it takes is a woman's careful touch.

Tilea is a wealthy land of many Princes, and many wealthy Princes in not enough land. With the return of the Besieger in Miragliano, the business-like Leonardo Catrazza opted for a cordial truce and to extend his enterprises elsewhere, while Borgio busied himself with punishing his enemies and defeating Ratmen and Greenskins who got too confident in his absence.\\n\\nWith his considerable assets and skills for diplomacy, Catrazza secured the large embassy in Shang-Yang just in time to see the Empire of Grand Cathay be compromised by its many external and internal threats. A man who could see opportunities even in a spent battlefield of dying men, Catrazza couldn't believe his luck at the panorama of chances laid all around him. The Iron Dragon, for the moment, trusts and respects Leonardo, whose talents and efficient mercenearies have served him before.\\n\\nComposed and erudite, Catrazza is by many considered a counterpart of Borgio in many things that make a Tilean Prince great. Where Borgio is ruthless and aggressive, Catrazza prefers less bloody initiatives. However, few forget that Leonardo is an accomplished duellist whose mind is as quick and lethal as his blades when need comes, and a commander with the trust of his men, both in his military skills and in his pockets. For all his soft speeches and unassuming behaviour, Catrazza always has a big stick in his pocket.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nAuthor's Note:\\nWhile not from the canon lore, this character's story and traits are a processed concoction derived from campaigns played by multiple people while he was the generic faction leader of his faction. In a way, these characters made themselves through their own actions.

Estalia lies in the south-western reaches of the Old World. Its local wealth is limited, its past and future one of conflict, its people one of stereotyped greed and contentiousness. Few of its small kingdoms and princedoms are powerful enough to make themselves known beyond the peninsula, though not for lack of trying, especially in rivalry against the Tilean neighbours and their crooked towers.\\n\\nMagritta is one of the most powerful cities in Estalia, and one that has the privilege of hosting much of the prominent Cult of Myrmidia, again poised in rivalry with their Tilean equivalents. Its ports and fleets are substantial and busy, once again in competition with neighbours from Bilbali, Tobaro, Miragliano, Remas and Luccini.\\n\\nIn the potential of this sunny city emerges Don Lupio, of the Sunscryer family. A controversial figure to everybody who knows him even from a safe distance, Lupio made his bid into becoming ruler of his city by getting rid of his brother, someone perhaps too good-natured to survive the competition. He then made himself notorious through his legendary greed for gold, his egocentricity and considerable talent for modern tactics; his strategic mind extends into vast panoramas of opportunism that have him happily wait for his allies' forces to be spent against a common enemy, before leading his fresh forces to defeat both and claim the entirety of both victory and spoils; particularly known among his subjects are his heavy taxes, eccentric behaviour and selective hatred towards peasantry and their mills. When fighting abroad, enemy Giants will be subject of his fury and concerted fire by his army, as he consistently believes them to be walking windmills.\\n\\nFor all of Lupio's faults, his foes are well-aware that behind the laughable masquerade of this El Dorado lies the mind of a shrewd general and politician. At least, when he feels inclined. Even his allies are careful not to underestimate him, as Lupio Sunscryer may well be the rising sun of a powerful Estalian kingdom, or the loudest and disastrous conflagration of Magritta's resources.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nAuthor's Note:\\nWhile not from the canon lore, this character's story and traits are a processed concoction derived from campaigns played by multiple people while he was the generic faction leader of his faction. In a way, these characters made themselves through their own actions.

The Border Princes are a region packed with a myriad of local domains, each the size of a crossroads or stretching to the horizon. Their rulers also range from a band of armed bandits to nobles and even vampires; a far cry from the powerful merchants and condottieri of Tilea or from the Counts of the Empire, and most of these autocrats are constantly at odds among each other and threatened by Beastmen or Greenskins.\\n\\nValmir Gausser is only one of such so-called Princes, one who got to his domain through a past of leading his own mercenary company. He distinguished himself among the normally-aloof Bretonnians and Dwarfs while fighting in Araby, from where he returned home with new scars, learned skills, useful friendships and a pegasus foal.\\n\\nHe quickly secured and expanded his own princedom, but the Borderlands are lethal for the incautious, and enough incoming doom to break most people. Gausser is surrounded by hungry neighbours and his lands have virtually-inexistent infrastructure compared to the most likely of his future foes. A man of his talents, who can be called Dwarf-Friend by the Dawi, who can count on the help of certain errant and crusading Lords, who can inspire his own soldiers by example and unsurpassed optimism, such man may just have what it takes to finally unit the Border Princes under the Renegade Crown. \\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nAuthor's Note:\\nWhile not from the canon lore, this character's story and traits are a processed concoction derived from campaigns played by multiple people while he was the generic faction leader of his faction. In a way, these characters made themselves through their own actions.

Forged in the constant mercenary warfare of Tilea, Cadavo is the product of the constant competition between various condottieri. With a penchant for practicality against mercy, Cadavo made enemies as quickly as he removed them, which includes the permanent enmity of a famous mercenary company, the Alcatani Fellowship. Always with an eye for opportunities, and perhaps to leave behind some more foes and debts, Cadavo is one of the most famous condottieri to ever lead forces into the New World, where lethal threats are as abundant as gold, artefacts and expensive spices. His talents did not include the necessary tact to make deals with the cold-blooded Lizardmen, which led to a one-sided and bloody feud between Cadavo and the scaly natives. A series of skirmishes that continued for so long and with such stubbornness demonstrated by this human interloper that it managed the impossible challenge of getting on Lord Mazdamundi's torpid nerves.\\n\\nRepeatedly a survivor of the cataclysmic interventions of the ancient Slann, Cadavo is quick to attract and hire more troops with which to push into the jungles and re-establish his own personal colony, which he called after himself. Cadavo's adventures in the remote world are famous and wide-spread.\\n\\nPerhaps even legendary. By the time of Karl Franz's coronation and much younger adventurers getting their feet wet and slightly-bitten in Lustria, Cadavo is still being seen fighting an endless war against the lizards who so unjustly kick his colony and enterprises into the dust. To the point that anyone with good sense has begun wondering whether Cadavo has indeed found a secret to immortality during his uneven struggles, or if the mantle of El Cadavo is being assumed by a succession of like-minded adventurers of singular charisma, stubbornness and greed.

Marco Colombo may not be the humblest among the many people who share his traits, but he sure accrues many of these talents. A Tilean condottiero like many others, Colombo is also an accomplished marksman, navigator, explorer, adventurer, commander, merchant, diplomat and the most fashionable in Lustria; at least, according to his biographers. Be as it may, his skills led him to become a famed general, the Prince of Trantio in Tilea, and one of the few beings in existence with a usable line of contacts with the Slanns of Lustria, or at least their Skink chiefs, a line that goes all the way up to Lord Mazdamundi himself nevertheless.\\n\\nNot unlike when treating with Dwarfs, a single faux pas can lead to not only economic collapse of a valuable trade line, but also utter destruction. Colombo is well-aware of the fact, and handles his contacts personally and carefully. In exchange for exorbitantly valuable items, Colombo leads his forces against any such marauding foe that the lethargic Lizardmen don't have the initiative to handle directly, such as Dark Elves or other pirates. With that in mind, Colombo also has little patience for other humans who constantly put his privileged trade partnership at risk with their callous greed, as opposed to his own well-managed fine taste.
Like Piggolo I of Tobaro, Prince Piggolo II is destined to lead his followers to a new golden age.
